transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things at work have gotten a little uncomfortable, and I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. Ever since I got that county safety award, some people at work seem to be… I don’t know, twisting my inspection reports, or reading them in a way that makes me look bad.

They’ve also been asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make it seem like I did something crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to be fair about that, but it really feels coordinated, like there’s an effort to discredit me. Does that make sense?
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately trying to discredit you?

I mean… “for certain” sounds a little strong, and I don’t want to sound unfair or paranoid or anything. But yes, I do think it’s deliberate. Ever since the county safety award, the way certain people have been handling my inspection reports and those budget questions… it doesn’t feel random.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to accept that, but I can tell there’s something coordinated there, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or discredit me. Does that answer it okay?
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I notice things other people might miss, maybe, but I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there. At least not that I’m aware of. Is that what you mean?
Outside of the situation at work, do you have other strong beliefs that people are trying to harm, watch, or plot against you?

No, not really outside of work. I don’t think people in general are out to get me or watching me or anything like that.

It’s more… this specific situation at work, after the county safety award. Certain people started twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, and it feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to be reasonable about it, but I can tell there’s something coordinated there.

I hope that makes sense. I’m not trying to sound dramatic.
How long have you been feeling that your coworkers are deliberately trying to discredit you?

It’s been… about a year, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but it started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That’s when I first started noticing the way people were acting with my reports and all that. So, yeah—around a year.
If your supervisor showed you clear proof that the report reviews and budget questions were routine and not directed at you, would you believe it?

I’d try to believe it. I mean, if he had clear proof, I wouldn’t want to just ignore that or be unreasonable.

But… honestly, I think I’d still wonder if I was only being shown part of it. Because from where I’m sitting, after that safety award, the way my reports started getting twisted and those budget questions came up… it really does feel coordinated, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. I know my supervisor says it’s routine, and maybe I’m supposed to accept that, but it’s hard to shake what I’ve been seeing.

Does that make sense? I’m not trying to be difficult.
Before this work situation, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t think so… not in a general way. I mean, I try to be careful with people, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say I walked around assuming people had bad motives.

Before all this, I thought I got along with people okay. Maybe I could be a little cautious sometimes, but not like… suspicious of everybody. Is that what you mean?
In your early adult life, long before this job issue, did you often suspect that other people were trying to use, harm, or deceive you?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not often. Maybe I was careful about who I trusted, but I didn’t go around thinking people were out to use me or hurt me.

At least, not that I remember. I don’t want to give the wrong answer, but this feels more tied to what’s been happening at work than something that’s always been there.
